column1: # Ancient Iranian targets (Chalcolithic, Bronze Age, Iron Age) modelled with the DISTAL design of Narasimhan et al. 2019 (SM S4.2.4):
# pre-Copper-Age ancestry components as rotating sources, a few fixed deep outgroups, p >= 0.01 and every weight +-2 SE inside [0,1].
# This is how the paper itself models ancient Copper Age and later populations. Use:
#   DESIGN=ancient_iran_distal sbatch --export=ALL run_qpwave_qpadm.sh          (targets come from THIS file: --targets config)
# TARGETS are grouped by site and archaeological period, as in the paper. Dates are from sample_meta.tsv (first sample of each label):
#   Hajji Firuz, NW Iran: IRN_HajjiFiruz_ChL ~6000-5890 BCE, Hajji_Firuz_C ~5890-5720 BCE (labelled Chalcolithic by the data source)
#   Tepe Hissar, N Iran: IRN_TepeHissar_ChL ~3640-3520 BCE, Tepe_Hissar_C ~2880-2640 BCE (pooled as in the paper; the date span is wide -> check homogeneity)
#   Shahr-i-Sokhta, SE Iran, Bronze Age: Shahr_I_Sokhta_BA1 ~2910-2880 BCE and IRN_Shahr_I_Sokhta_BA ~2600-2500 BCE (kept as two groups; the paper shows this
#       site contains more than one ancestry profile)
#   Hasanlu, NW Iran: Bronze Age IRN_Hasanlu_MBA ~2200-2030, LBA_A ~1425-1285, LBA_B ~1495-1325 BCE (1 sample each, pooled, exploratory);
#   Dinkha Tepe, NW Iran, Bronze/Iron Age: IRN_DinkhaTepe_BIA_A (6) and BIA_B (8, ~1880-1690 BCE), the two published clusters
# Singletons (IRN_HajjiFiruz_BA, IRN_HajjiFiruz_IA) are excluded, as the paper excludes single-individual groups from primary analyses.
# Ganj_Dareh_N (Iran_N) is a SOURCE here, not a target.
